t: This is the Garrick Theatre, a West End playhouse on Charing Cross Road. It takes its name from the actor David Garrick, a friend and pupil of Samuel Johnson, who wrote, produced and shaped much of eighteenth-century theatre. The building was designed by Walter Emden, one of the leading theatre architects of his day, for the dramatist W. S. Gilbert. It opened in 1889 with John Hare's production of Pinero's The Profligate. Another Pinero play, The Notorious Mrs. Ebbsmith, was an early success and scandalised some of the audience.
